import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML

# Helper to compare expected output for typical HTML entities
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str, expected",
    [
        (None, None),
        ("", ""),
        ("plain text", "plain text"),
        ("&", "&"),
        ("<div>", "<div>"),
        ("a & b < c", "a & b < c"),
        ("&foo<", "&foo<"),  # problematic case: internal '&' should not be swallowed
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_behaviour(input_str, expected):
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected

def test_unescapeHTML_assertion_error():
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError):
        unescapeHTML(123)  # not a compat_str

def test_unescapeHTML_multiple_entities():
    s = "&Hello &World<test>"Sample""
    expected = "&Hello &World<test>\"Sample\""
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected

def test_unescapeHTML_entity_with_extra_ampersand_inside():
    # This string contains an extra '&' between two valid entities.
    # Old implementation would decode both entities separately.
    # New implementation must not treat the whole string as a single unknown entity.
    s = "&foo&lt;"
    expected = "&foo<"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected
